en: to make gimchi; to make kimchi for the winter

examples.en: The family gathers to make winter kimchi.
This weekend we made winter kimchi at Grandma's house.

examples.ko: 올해는 배추 오십 포기로 김장할 거예요.
examples.en: This year I'll make winter kimchi with fifty heads of cabbage.
On kimjang day, we eat boiled pork.

examples.ko: 요즘은 김장하지 않고 사 먹는 집도 많아요.
examples.en: These days many households buy kimchi instead of making it.

examples.ko: 어머니와 같이 김장하는 게 힘들지만 즐거워요.
examples.en: Making winter kimchi with my mother is tiring but fun.

explain: 그냥 김치를 담글 때는 '김치를 담그다'라고 하고, 늦가을에 겨울 동안 먹을 김치를 한꺼번에 많이 담글 때만 '김장하다'라고 해요. 이웃과 나눠 먹는 한국의 김장 문화는 유네스코 무형유산이에요.

phrases.en: We make kimchi for winter with family this year too.
phrases.nuance_ko: '김장하다'를 띄어서 말하는 형태로, 뜻은 같아요.
phrases.nuance_en: The spaced form of 김장하다, with the same meaning.

phrases.en: Cabbage prices go up in kimchi-making season.
phrases.nuance_ko: 늦가을에 김장을 하는 때를 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: The late-autumn season when people make winter kimchi.

phrases.en: The winter kimchi has ripened nicely.
phrases.nuance_ko: 김장해서 만든 김치를 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: Kimchi made during 김장.

explain_en: Making ordinary kimchi is '김치를 담그다'; '김장하다' is only for making a large batch in late autumn to last the winter. Korea's kimjang culture of sharing with neighbors is on UNESCO's intangible heritage list.

examples.en: Neobiani was served on the feast table.
I could smell my mother grilling neobiani.

examples.ko: 이 한식 도시락에는 너비아니가 들어 있어요.
examples.en: This Korean lunch box has neobiani in it.
The kids like neobiani the most.
Neobiani and rice alone make a filling meal.
For lunch today I'll have the neobiani set meal.

explain: 양념한 소고기를 넓적하게 저며 구운 한국 음식이에요. 불고기와 비슷하다고 생각하는 사람이 많지만, 잔치나 도시락 반찬처럼 한 점씩 집어 먹는 구이로 많이 나와요.

phrases.en: I grilled neobiani and ate it for dinner.
phrases.nuance_ko: 음식을 직접 만들어 먹는다고 말할 때 쓰는 가장 기본적인 표현이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: The most basic phrase for saying you cook the dish yourself.

phrases.en: I packed neobiani as a side dish in my lunch box.
phrases.nuance_ko: 밥과 함께 먹는 반찬으로 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used when talking about it as a side dish to eat with rice.

phrases.en: The neobiani is tender and delicious.
phrases.nuance_ko: 음식 맛을 말할 때 쓰는 기본 형태예요.
phrases.nuance_en: The basic form for talking about how the dish tastes.

explain_en: It is a Korean dish of seasoned beef cut into broad slices and grilled. Many people think of it as similar to bulgogi, but it often appears as a grilled side dish eaten piece by piece, as at feasts or in lunch boxes.

en: particularly good taste; food with particularly good taste

examples.en: In this region, oyster pancakes are the winter specialty.
Cold noodles are a summer treat.

examples.ko: 비 오는 날 김치전은 최고의 별미 같아요.
examples.en: On a rainy day, kimchi pancakes feel like the best treat.

examples.ko: 여행 가면 그 지역 별미를 꼭 먹어 봐요.
examples.en: When I travel, I always try the local specialty.
Even cup noodles are a treat when I eat them once in a while.

examples.ko: 별미로 먹는 간식이라 평소엔 안 만들어요.
examples.en: It's a snack for special occasions, so I don't usually make it.

explain: 평소에 먹는 밥이 아니라 특별히 맛있게 느껴지는 음식에 써요. 그 계절이나 그 지역에서만 맛볼 수 있는 음식에도 자주 써요. '별식'(특별한 음식)과도 가까운 말이에요.

phrases.en: In summer, I eat cold soy milk noodles as a special treat.
phrases.nuance_ko: 평소 밥이 아니라 특별히 즐기는 음식일 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used for food enjoyed as a special treat rather than a regular meal.

phrases.en: On weekends, we make kalguksu as a special dish.
phrases.nuance_ko: '별미'와 가까운 말로, 특별히 만들어 먹는 음식을 가리켜요.
phrases.nuance_en: Close to 별미; it refers to food made as a special meal.

phrases.example: 여행 가면 그 지역 별미를 꼭 먹어 봐요.
phrases.en: When I travel, I always try the local specialty.
phrases.nuance_ko: 그 지역에서만 맛볼 수 있는 음식을 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used for food you can only enjoy in that region.

explain_en: It refers to food that tastes especially good compared with everyday meals, and it is often used for seasonal or regional dishes. It is close in meaning to '별식' (a special dish).

examples.ko: 싼 게 비지떡이라더니 가방이 금방 망가졌어요.
examples.en: They say cheap things are no good, and sure enough the bag broke quickly.
The bijitteok my grandmother made for me was warm.
I bought bijitteok at the market and ate it as a snack.

examples.ko: 어릴 때 비지떡을 자주 먹었다고 하셨어요.
examples.en: He said he often ate bijitteok when he was little.

examples.ko: 비지떡 한 조각에 따뜻한 차를 마셨어요.
examples.en: I had a piece of bijitteok with a cup of hot tea.
I bought it because it was cheap, but it was worthless.

explain: 음식 이름이지만 속담 '싼 게 비지떡'으로도 알려져 있어요. 값싼 물건을 샀다가 품질이 나빠 후회할 때 '비지떡이었다'처럼 비유로 말하기도 해요.

phrases.example: 싼 게 비지떡이라고 하잖아요. 너무 싼 물건은 조심하세요.
phrases.en: They say you get what you pay for. Be careful with things that are too cheap.
phrases.nuance_ko: 값이 싼 물건은 품질도 그만큼 떨어진다는 뜻의 속담이에요. 싼 물건을 샀다가 실망했을 때 자주 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: A proverb meaning that cheap goods tend to be low in quality. People often say it when disappointed after buying something cheap.
phrases.en_equiv: you get what you pay for

explain_en: It is the name of a food, but it is also known through the proverb '싼 게 비지떡'. When you buy something cheap and regret its poor quality, you can say '비지떡이었다' figuratively.

examples.en: On cold days I crave a hot bowl of seonjitguk.

examples.ko: 이 식당 선짓국은 국물이 진하고 맛있어요.
examples.en: The seonjitguk at this restaurant has a rich, tasty broth.
I put rice in the seonjitguk and ate it.
I miss the seonjitguk my mother used to cook.
It's my first time having seonjitguk, but it's surprisingly good.
I ordered a bowl of seonjitguk and some kimchi.

explain: 소의 피를 굳힌 '선지'를 넣고 끓인 국이에요. 처음 먹는 사람은 호불호가 갈려요. 식당에서는 '선지국'이라고도 말해요.

phrases.en: This restaurant is famous for its tasty blood soup.
phrases.nuance_ko: '선짓국'과 같은 음식이고 식당에서는 이렇게도 많이 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: It is the same dish as 선짓국, and restaurants often say it this way too.

phrases.en: Boss, one bowl of blood soup, please.
phrases.nuance_ko: 식당에서 주문할 때 바로 쓸 수 있는 말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: You can use this directly when ordering at a restaurant.

phrases.en: My mother made blood soup for me on the weekend.
phrases.nuance_ko: 집에서 국을 만드는 상황에서는 '끓이다'와 함께 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: For cooking soup at home, use it with 끓이다.

explain_en: It is a soup made with '선지', congealed beef blood. People who try it for the first time often either love it or dislike it. At restaurants it is also called '선지국'.

examples.en: I tried sea urchin seaweed soup in Jeju.

examples.ko: 성게는 가시가 많아서 조심해서 만져야 해요.
examples.en: Sea urchins have many spines, so you must touch them carefully.
I saw a person catching sea urchins at the beach.
This sea urchin roe is nutty and sweet, so it's delicious.
A sea urchin is stuck between the rocks.
This restaurant is famous for its sea urchin bibimbap.

explain: 먹는 부분은 '성게알'이라고 불러서 메뉴에는 '성게알'이라고 적힌 경우도 많아요. 가시가 있는 바다 동물이라 바닷가에서 만지면 위험할 수 있어요.

phrases.en: This restaurant is famous for its sea urchin roe bibimbap.
phrases.nuance_ko: 먹는 부분을 가리키는 이름이라서 메뉴에 자주 나와요.
phrases.nuance_en: The name of the edible part, often seen on menus.

phrases.en: It hurts if you get pricked by sea urchin spines.
phrases.nuance_ko: 바닷가에서 조심하라고 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used when warning people at the seaside.

phrases.en: We went into the sea and caught sea urchins.
phrases.nuance_ko: 해녀나 바닷가 체험에서 자주 나오는 쓰임이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: Common when talking about divers or seaside activities.

explain_en: The edible part is called '성게알' (sea urchin roe), so menus often use that word. It is a spiny sea animal, so touching one at the beach can be dangerous.

examples.en: After drinking cold omija tea, my thirst went away.

examples.ko: 오미자는 여러 가지 맛이 다 난다고 해요.
examples.en: They say omija has several different tastes all at once.

examples.ko: 시골 할머니가 오미자를 말려서 보내 주셨어요.
examples.en: My grandmother in the countryside dried omija and sent it to me.

examples.ko: 여름에는 오미자 화채를 자주 만들어 먹어요.
examples.en: In summer I often make and eat omija punch.

examples.ko: 가을에는 시장에 빨간 오미자가 많이 나와요.
examples.en: In autumn, lots of red omija show up at the market.

examples.ko: 오미자에 꿀을 넣어서 차게 마셔 봤어요.
examples.en: I put honey in omija and drank it cold.

explain: 열매 이름이고 '오미자차', '오미자청'처럼 음료로 많이 먹어요. 한자로는 다섯 가지 맛(五味)이라는 뜻이라서 맛이 여러 가지라고 말해요.

phrases.example: 감기 기운이 있을 때 따뜻한 오미자차를 마셔요.
phrases.en: I drink warm omija tea when I feel a cold coming on.
phrases.nuance_ko: 오미자 열매로 우린 차로, 가장 흔한 쓰임이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: A tea made from the berries, and the most common use.

phrases.en: I mixed omija syrup with water and drank it.
phrases.nuance_ko: 오미자를 설탕에 절여 만든 달콤한 액체예요.
phrases.nuance_en: A sweet syrup made by steeping the berries in sugar.

phrases.en: Eating omija punch in summer is refreshing.
phrases.nuance_ko: 오미자 국물에 과일을 띄운 한국 전통 음료예요.
phrases.nuance_en: A traditional Korean drink with fruit floating in omija liquid.

explain_en: It is the name of a berry and is often enjoyed as a drink, such as '오미자차' or '오미자청'. In Chinese characters it means 'five flavors' (五味), which is why people say it tastes of several things at once.

examples.en: The child crunches away on a cucumber.

examples.ko: 형이 과자를 우적우적 먹으면서 영화를 봐요.
examples.en: My brother watches a movie while munching on snacks.
The horse is chomping on grass.
I was so hungry that I wolfed down the bread.
If you crunch ice, your teeth hurt.
He took a big crunchy bite of the apple.

explain: 단단하거나 질긴 것을 거칠게 씹는 소리와 모양에 써요. '아삭아삭'은 신선한 채소나 과일의 가벼운 식감이고, '우물우물'은 입 안에서 천천히 씹는 모양이라 서로 달라요.

phrases.en: The child chews a carrot noisily.
phrases.nuance_ko: 단단한 것을 힘차게 씹는 가장 흔한 짝말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: The most common pairing for chewing something hard with force.

phrases.en: My younger brother eats snacks crunching loudly.
phrases.nuance_ko: 소리 내며 거칠게 먹는 모습을 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: It describes eating in a rough, noisy way.

phrases.example: 방 안에서 우적우적 씹는 소리가 들려요.
phrases.en: I can hear crunching sounds in the room.
phrases.nuance_ko: 씹을 때 나는 소리 자체를 가리킬 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Use it to refer to the sound of chewing itself.

explain_en: It describes the sound and look of chewing hard or tough food roughly. '아삭아삭' is the light crispness of fresh vegetables or fruit, and '우물우물' is slow chewing in the mouth, so they differ.

examples.en: The players on the winning team are full of confidence.
That person who had been so full of vigor suddenly got quiet.
He walked into the meeting room with a swaggering look.
When they took the lead, the opposing team became cocky.
He boasted loudly and confidently, but ended up making a mistake.
At first he was full of vigor, but soon he lost heart.

explain: 기운이 대단하고 당당한 모습을 말해요. '기고만장하다'와 비슷하지만 '기고만장하다'가 잘난 척하는 느낌이 더 강해요. 승리하거나 힘이 생겼을 때 사람이나 팀에게 많이 써요.

phrases.en: They entered the stadium looking full of confidence.
phrases.nuance_ko: 당당하고 힘이 넘치는 겉모습을 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: Describes a proud and powerful appearance.

phrases.en: He spoke in a high-spirited, confident way.
phrases.nuance_ko: '-게'를 붙이면 동사를 꾸며요.
phrases.nuance_en: With -게, it modifies a verb.

phrases.en: You shouldn't get cocky just because you won.
phrases.nuance_ko: '기세등등하다'보다 잘난 척하는 느낌이 강해요.
phrases.nuance_en: Has a stronger sense of boasting than 기세등등하다.

explain_en: It describes an imposing, confident energy. It is similar to '기고만장하다', but that word feels more like showing off. It is often used for a person or team that has won or gained power.

examples.ko: 이 유리는 불투명해서 안이 안 보여요.
examples.en: This glass is opaque, so you cannot see inside.

examples.ko: 안이 안 보이게 불투명한 봉투에 담아 주세요.
examples.en: Please put it in an opaque bag so the inside cannot be seen.
The economic outlook is still uncertain.
If the schedule is unclear, postpone the reservation.

examples.ko: 불투명하게 코팅된 창문은 햇빛을 막아 줘요.
examples.en: Windows with an opaque coating block sunlight.

examples.ko: 결과가 불투명했던 일이 잘 끝나서 다행이에요.
examples.en: I am glad the thing with an uncertain outcome ended well.

explain: 유리나 비닐처럼 안이 안 보이는 물건에도 쓰고, 앞날이나 상황이 분명하지 않을 때도 써요. 반대는 '투명하다'예요. '운영이 불투명하다'처럼 과정이 공개되지 않아 믿기 어렵다는 뜻으로도 말해요.

phrases.example: 욕실 창문은 불투명한 유리로 되어 있어요.
phrases.en: The bathroom window is made of opaque glass.
phrases.nuance_ko: 안이 안 보이는 물건을 꾸밀 때 쓰는 가장 기본적인 짝말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: The most basic collocation for things you can't see through.

phrases.en: The economy is bad, so the company's future is uncertain.
phrases.nuance_ko: 앞으로의 일이 분명하지 않을 때 비유로 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used figuratively when the future is unclear.

phrases.en: The plan changed, so the schedule became unclear.
phrases.nuance_ko: 상황이 점점 분명하지 않게 되는 변화를 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: Describes a situation gradually becoming unclear.

explain_en: It describes things you cannot see through, like glass or plastic, and also a future or situation that is unclear. The opposite is '투명하다'. It can also mean a process is not open enough to be trusted, as in '운영이 불투명하다'.

examples.en: I wore a pale pink dress.
The clouds are thin today, so the sun shines through.

examples.ko: 커피 색이 너무 엷어서 맛이 싱거워요.
examples.en: The coffee color is too light and it tastes weak.

examples.ko: 엷은 안개가 아침 산을 덮고 있었어요.
examples.en: A thin mist covered the mountain in the morning.
Her makeup is light, so she looks natural.
As the sunlight thinned, evening came.

explain: '엷다'는 색이나 빛, 안개, 화장이 진하지 않을 때 써요. '얇다'는 두께가 작은 물건에, '엷다'는 진하기가 약할 때 써서 달라요. 반대말은 '짙다'이고, 말할 때는 '연하다'가 더 흔해요.

phrases.en: I like light makeup.
phrases.nuance_ko: 명사 앞에서 '엷은'으로 바뀌어 진하지 않은 것을 꾸며 줘요.
phrases.nuance_en: Changes to 엷은 before a noun to describe something not strong.

phrases.en: I painted the wall lightly.
phrases.nuance_ko: '엷게'는 색을 진하지 않게 할 때 동사 앞에 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: 엷게 goes before a verb to mean not too dark.

phrases.en: This color isn't very light.
phrases.nuance_ko: 부정형으로 색이 꽤 진하다는 뜻을 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: The negative form says the color is fairly strong.

explain_en: 엷다 is used when color, light, mist, or makeup is not strong. 얇다 is for physical thickness, while 엷다 is for lightness of intensity. The opposite is 짙다, and in speech 연하다 is more common.

t90.ax: I wore a pale pink dress.

en: to be bumpy; to be rough; to be knotty

examples.en: The wall is bumpy, so it feels rough to the touch.

examples.ko: 얼음이 녹았다가 다시 얼어서 우툴두툴한 표면이 그리 미끄럽지는 않았어요.
examples.en: The ice melted and refroze, so the bumpy surface wasn't very slippery.
My facial skin became bumpy, so I went to the hospital.
The road is bumpy, so walk carefully.
The cucumber skin is bumpy, but it tastes good.

examples.ko: 이 돌은 표면이 우툴두툴하게 깎여 있어요.
examples.en: This stone has been cut with a rough, bumpy surface.

explain: '울퉁불퉁하다'가 길이나 땅처럼 크게 굴곡진 곳에 어울린다면, '우툴두툴하다'는 피부, 오이 껍질, 벽처럼 작은 돌기가 많은 표면에 더 잘 어울려요. 반대말은 '매끈하다'예요.

phrases.en: I'm worried about my skin, which is bumpy like cucumber peel.
phrases.nuance_ko: 명사 앞에 붙여 작은 돌기가 많은 표면을 표현해요.
phrases.nuance_en: Before a noun, it describes a surface with many small bumps.

phrases.example: 이 벽은 가까이서 보면 우툴두툴해 보여요.
phrases.en: This wall looks rough up close.
phrases.nuance_ko: 눈에 보이는 표면 모양을 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Use it for how a surface looks to the eye.

phrases.en: The road is uneven, so it's hard to walk.
phrases.nuance_ko: '우툴두툴하다'보다 크게 굴곡진 길이나 땅에 더 잘 어울려요.
phrases.nuance_en: Fits big uneven areas like roads better than 우툴두툴하다.

explain_en: '울퉁불퉁하다' suits roads and ground with big dips and bumps, while '우툴두툴하다' fits surfaces with many small bumps, such as skin, cucumber peel or walls. The opposite is '매끈하다' (smooth).

en: to be strange; to be queer

examples.en: Hearing that story gives me a strange feeling.
There's a weird smell coming from the room.
The scene I saw in my dream was so strange.

examples.ko: 그 사람이 저를 이상야릇하게 쳐다봐서 불편했어요.
examples.en: That person looked at me in an odd way, so I felt uncomfortable.
It's a food with a strange taste, but I keep thinking about it.
Doesn't this picture look a bit strange?

explain: '이상하다'보다 느낌을 더 강조해서, 묘하고 낯설어서 딱 집어 말하기 어려운 기분이나 분위기에 써요. 기분, 냄새, 표정, 분위기와 잘 어울려요. 비슷한 말로 '야릇하다'도 있어요.

phrases.en: A strange, odd atmosphere filled the room.
phrases.nuance_ko: 명사 앞에서 꾸미는 활용이고, 뭐라 말하기 어려운 분위기에 어울려요.
phrases.nuance_en: The modifier form, fitting an atmosphere that's hard to describe.

phrases.en: That person's smile is somehow strange.
phrases.nuance_ko: 해요체로 지금 느끼는 묘한 기분을 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: Polite form for a strange feeling you have right now.

phrases.en: I feel odd, so I can't sleep.
phrases.nuance_ko: 더 짧은 말로, 묘하고 이상한 느낌을 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: A shorter word for a curious, odd feeling.

explain_en: It adds more emphasis than '이상하다', and fits a feeling or atmosphere that is oddly unfamiliar and hard to pin down. It goes well with words like mood, smell, expression, and atmosphere. '야릇하다' is a similar word.

t90.ax: Doesn't this picture look a bit strange?

en: to be carefree; to be easygoing (in manner)

examples.en: Even in a crisis, he is smiling without a care.
It's the day before the exam. How can you be so carefree?

examples.ko: 동생은 태평스러운 성격이라 걱정을 잘 안 해요.
examples.en: My younger sibling has a carefree personality and rarely worries.
Even my always carefree friend was nervous this time.

examples.ko: 저 사람은 태평스러워 보이지만 속으로는 많이 고민해요.
examples.en: He looks carefree, but he worries a lot inside.

examples.ko: 아빠는 늘 태평스럽지만 일은 꼼꼼하게 하세요.
examples.en: Dad is always easygoing, but he does his work carefully.

explain: '태평하다'와 비슷하지만 걱정할 만한 상황에서도 느긋해 보이는 모습이나 태도를 말할 때 더 잘 어울려요. 때로는 '왜 이렇게 걱정이 없어?' 하는 놀라움이나 핀잔이 섞여요. 'ㅂ' 불규칙이라 '태평스러워요', '태평스러운'으로 바뀌어요.

phrases.en: Even in a crisis, he has a carefree look on his face.
phrases.nuance_ko: 'ㅂ' 불규칙이라 꾸밈말은 '태평스러운'이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: Because it is ㅂ-irregular, the modifier form is '태평스러운'.

phrases.en: The day before the exam, you look so carefree.
phrases.nuance_ko: 겉모습이 느긋해 보인다고 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used when someone looks relaxed on the outside.

phrases.example: 그는 큰 실수를 하고도 태평스럽게 말해요.
phrases.en: Even after a big mistake, he speaks so casually.
phrases.nuance_ko: 걱정할 일에도 느긋한 말투를 가리킬 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Describes a relaxed way of speaking about something worrying.

explain_en: It is close to '태평하다', but it fits better when someone looks relaxed even in a situation that calls for worry. It can carry a hint of surprise or mild scolding, like 'how can you be so carefree?'. It is a ㅂ-irregular word, so it becomes '태평스러워요' and '태평스러운'.

p.n: -스럽다 describes how someone appears; 태평하다 states it directly.

t90.ax: Even in a crisis, he is smiling without a care.
